properties.title: NX-400 Technical Specification — Hardware Revision 1
properties.installationRequirements:
The NX-400 is a floor-standing pedestal unit requiring a dedicated three-phase 400V, 63A circuit sized for simultaneous dual-socket operation. Foundation and cable-routing requirements follow standard pedestal-charger practice; confirm available capacity for dynamic load balancing across multiple NX-400 units before finalizing circuit sizing if more than one unit shares a supply.

Routine preventive maintenance is recommended every twelve months for standard-duty sites, or every six months for sites averaging more than one hundred charging sessions per month, covering connector wear inspection, residual-current-device and breaker function testing, enclosure seal condition, and confirmation that the unit is running current firmware.
properties.safetyInformation: Installation and service must be performed by a qualified, certified electrician. Dynamic load balancing configuration should only be adjusted by personnel trained on the Polaris Charge Cloud platform, since an incorrect shared-circuit budget can lead to nuisance breaker trips under load.
properties.certificationInformation: CE marked; complies with applicable low-voltage, EMC, and OCPP 2.0.1 conformance requirements.
properties.techNotes:
Firmware for this hardware revision has progressed through the 4.x line since 2023. Version 4.8 introduced an intermittent OCPP backend disconnect (E217) on dual-socket units under sustained high session volume after roughly 72 hours of continuous uptime; this was fixed in 4.8.1. See SPEC-NX400-02 for the current recommended firmware baseline and KI-NX400-004 for full detail on E217.

Service response for units under this specification follows Northstar's standard Essential, Professional, and Gold plan tiers. Gold-tier customers receive a 30-minute critical remote response target, with four-hour on-site response in supported metropolitan areas and eight-hour response elsewhere.
properties.tags: NX-400, hardware spec, dual-socket, OCPP 2.0.1

properties.title: NX-100 Technical Specification — Hardware Revision 1
properties.installationRequirements:
The NX-100 mounts to an interior or exterior wall on a single-phase 230V, 32A dedicated circuit. No dedicated transformer or three-phase supply is required. Allow standard clearance around the unit for cable access and ventilation, and terminate the network connection (Ethernet, or configure Wi-Fi during commissioning) before energizing the circuit.

Routine preventive maintenance is recommended every twelve months for standard-duty sites, or every six months for sites averaging more than one hundred charging sessions per month, covering connector wear inspection, residual-current-device and breaker function testing, enclosure seal condition, and confirmation that the unit is running current firmware.
properties.safetyInformation: Installation and any internal service must be performed by a qualified, certified electrician familiar with local wiring regulations. Do not open the enclosure while the unit is energized. The circuit supplying the NX-100 must include appropriate residual-current protection sized per local code before the unit is commissioned.
properties.certificationInformation: CE marked; complies with applicable low-voltage and EMC directives for the countries in which it is sold. IP54 enclosure rating verified for outdoor wall-mount use.
properties.techNotes:
Rev 1 is the original NX-100 hardware build and remains the current shipping revision; no Rev 2 has been released to date.

Service response for units under this specification follows Northstar's standard Essential, Professional, and Gold plan tiers. Gold-tier customers receive a 30-minute critical remote response target, with four-hour on-site response in supported metropolitan areas and eight-hour response elsewhere.
properties.tags: NX-100, hardware spec, single-phase, wall-mount

properties.title: NX-200 Technical Specification — Hardware Revision 1 (Superseded)
properties.installationRequirements:
Rev 1 requires a dedicated three-phase 400V, 32A circuit and standard wall or pedestal mounting clearance. The RFID reader module was a factory-fit-only option on Rev 1 and could not be retrofitted in the field.

Routine preventive maintenance is recommended every twelve months for standard-duty sites, or every six months for sites averaging more than one hundred charging sessions per month, covering connector wear inspection, residual-current-device and breaker function testing, enclosure seal condition, and confirmation that the unit is running current firmware.
properties.safetyInformation: Installation and service require a qualified, certified electrician. The supply circuit must include appropriate three-phase protection devices sized per local code.
properties.certificationInformation: CE marked under the certification in effect at Rev 1's release; superseded by the Rev 2 certification package below, which extends the rated operating temperature range.
properties.techNotes:
This is the original NX-200 hardware revision, shipped from launch in 2022 until Rev 2's release. It is superseded by SPEC-NX200-02, which widened the operating temperature range and made the RFID reader field-installable. Existing Rev 1 units in service remain supported; new orders ship as Rev 2.

properties.title: NX-200 Technical Specification — Hardware Revision 2 (Current)
properties.installationRequirements:
Rev 2 requires the same dedicated three-phase 400V, 32A circuit as Rev 1. Unlike Rev 1, the RFID reader and 4G modules are both field-installable add-ons and no longer require factory fitment, simplifying post-installation upgrades.

Routine preventive maintenance is recommended every twelve months for standard-duty sites, or every six months for sites averaging more than one hundred charging sessions per month, covering connector wear inspection, residual-current-device and breaker function testing, enclosure seal condition, and confirmation that the unit is running current firmware.
properties.safetyInformation: Installation and service require a qualified, certified electrician. The supply circuit must include appropriate three-phase protection devices sized per local code.
properties.certificationInformation:
CE marked; extends the certified operating temperature range to -25°C to +50°C compared with Rev 1's -20°C to +45°C range.

Replacement RFID reader modules and 4G modem add-on kits for Rev 2 are stocked as standard spare parts, reflecting their field-installable design; Rev 1 units requiring these components must be scheduled for a factory-fit service visit instead.
properties.techNotes:
Rev 2 is the current shipping hardware revision, superseding SPEC-NX200-01. Field-installable RFID and 4G modules were the main driver for the revision, along with the widened operating temperature certification.

Service response for units under this specification follows Northstar's standard Essential, Professional, and Gold plan tiers. Gold-tier customers receive a 30-minute critical remote response target, with four-hour on-site response in supported metropolitan areas and eight-hour response elsewhere.

properties.installationRequirements:

properties.maximumPower: 2 x 22 kW (prototype, derated to 2x18 kW in early test units)
properties.connectivity: Ethernet only; 4G modem not yet integrated in prototype build
properties.installationRequirements:
This specification documents the internal pre-launch prototype build used during NX-400 development and field trials in 2022 and early 2023. It does not reflect the shipping product and is retained for historical reference only; no new installations should be planned against it.

properties.safetyInformation: As an archived, non-shipping specification, this document should not be used to guide any live installation. Any prototype-era unit still in a test environment must only be serviced by qualified, certified personnel aware of its non-production status.
properties.certificationInformation: The prototype build was not CE certified for commercial sale; certification was completed only for the shipping Rev 1 hardware described in SPEC-NX400-01.
properties.techNotes:
Retained for historical/engineering reference only. Key differences from the shipping product: no integrated 4G modem, OCPP 1.6J rather than 2.0.1, a lower IP44 enclosure rating, and a narrower 0°C to +40°C operating range. All of these were addressed before the Rev 1 commercial launch.

properties.safetyInformation: Installation and service must be performed by a qualified, certified electrician. As with the NX-400, dynamic load balancing configuration should only be adjusted by personnel trained on Polaris Charge Cloud.

Sites billing per kWh should confirm units are running 1.2 or later.

properties.installationRequirements:
The DX-60 requires a dedicated three-phase 400V supply at approximately 100A. Unlike the higher-power DX units, most sites can accommodate a DX-60 on existing distribution-board capacity without a dedicated transformer, though a site survey should still confirm available headroom before installation.

Routine preventive maintenance is recommended every twelve months for standard-duty sites, or every six months for sites averaging more than one hundred charging sessions per month, covering connector wear inspection, residual-current-device and breaker function testing, enclosure seal condition, and confirmation that the unit is running current firmware.
properties.safetyInformation: Installation and service must be performed by a qualified, certified electrician experienced with DC fast-charging equipment. The unit's DC output stage must never be serviced while energized; follow lockout-tagout procedure before opening the cabinet.
properties.certificationInformation:
CE marked; complies with applicable low-voltage, EMC, and OCPP 2.0.1 conformance requirements for DC fast-charging equipment.

Replacement CCS2 gun and cable assemblies are stocked as standard spare parts; a gun replacement can generally be completed within a single service visit without removing the main cabinet from service for more than the duration of the swap.
properties.techNotes:
Rev 1 is the original and current shipping hardware for the DX-60; no subsequent hardware revision has been released.

properties.title: DX-240 Technical Specification — Modular Hardware Revision 1
properties.installationRequirements:
The DX-240 requires a dedicated three-phase 400V supply at approximately 350A — roughly double the DX-120's requirement, reflecting its two-module design. Installation prerequisites (dedicated transformer room, cable routing, clearances) closely resemble the DX-120's, sized for the higher current rating. A detailed site survey confirming grid capacity should be completed before scheduling installation.

Routine preventive maintenance is recommended every twelve months for standard-duty sites, or every six months for sites averaging more than one hundred charging sessions per month, covering connector wear inspection, residual-current-device and breaker function testing, enclosure seal condition, and confirmation that the unit is running current firmware.
properties.safetyInformation: Installation and service must be performed by a qualified, certified electrician experienced with high-current, multi-module DC fast-charging systems. Each power module must be individually isolated via lockout-tagout before internal service; do not assume isolating one module de-energizes the other.
properties.certificationInformation: CE marked; complies with applicable low-voltage, EMC, and OCPP 2.0.1 conformance requirements for modular high-power DC fast-charging systems.
properties.techNotes:
The modular architecture means a fault in one 120 kW module degrades total capacity rather than taking the system fully offline — the surviving module continues serving connected guns at reduced throughput until the faulty module is serviced.

Substation and module isolation procedures must both be followed via lockout-tagout before any internal service — do not treat module-level isolation as sufficient on its own given the upstream MV/LV infrastructure.

properties.techNotes:

properties.title: Polaris Charge Cloud Technical Specification — System Requirements & Integration
properties.connectivity: HTTPS/TLS 1.2+, OCPP 1.6J/2.0.1 charger connections, REST API
properties.protocols: OCPP 1.6J, OCPP 2.0.1, OAuth2 client credentials (API Management module)
properties.installationRequirements:
Polaris Charge Cloud is delivered as a SaaS platform with no on-premises server component to install. Chargers connect outbound over OCPP to the Polaris backend, so on-site requirements are limited to confirming that the site's network allows outbound OCPP/HTTPS traffic and, for the API Management module, provisioning OAuth2 client credentials for any integrating system.

Because this is a SaaS platform rather than physical equipment, there is no on-site maintenance schedule; instead, customers integrating against its API should review release notes at each version boundary and re-test integration credentials whenever OAuth2 client-credentials rotation is due, typically on the same cadence as the customer's own internal security policy requires.
properties.safetyInformation: No electrical safety considerations apply to the software platform itself. However, any configuration change to dynamic load balancing or charging priority rules made through Polaris directly affects connected hardware behavior, and such changes should only be made by personnel trained on the platform to avoid unintended load-management outcomes.

properties.title: Atlas Fleet Technical Specification — System Requirements & Integration
properties.connectivity: HTTPS/TLS 1.2+; integrates with Polaris Charge Cloud for charger telemetry
properties.protocols: REST API integration with Polaris Charge Cloud
properties.installationRequirements:
Atlas Fleet is delivered as a SaaS platform with no on-premises component. It requires an active Polaris Charge Cloud deployment to source charger telemetry and session data; no direct charger connection is made by Atlas itself.

Because this is a SaaS platform rather than physical equipment, there is no on-site maintenance schedule; instead, customers integrating against its API should review release notes at each version boundary and re-test integration credentials whenever OAuth2 client-credentials rotation is due, typically on the same cadence as the customer's own internal security policy requires.
properties.safetyInformation: No electrical safety considerations apply to the software platform. Fleet managers configuring route or scheduling rules should be aware that Atlas's charge-scheduling recommendations are advisory unless explicitly enforced through Polaris; the platform does not directly override charger-level controls.
properties.certificationInformation: Not applicable — Atlas Fleet is a fleet-management application rather than charging hardware or protocol-conformant equipment.
properties.techNotes:
Atlas depends on Polaris for underlying charger status and session data, which keeps its release cadence independent of charger firmware versions. Route Optimization requires Atlas 2.2 or later; the driver mobile app v2 shipped in the 2.3 release.

properties.maximumPower: Up to 500 kW (modular, target 4 x 125 kW — subject to change)

properties.outputVoltage: 150-1000V DC (preliminary), CCS2 connectors, gun count not yet finalized
properties.protocols: OCPP 2.0.1 (planned); megawatt charging system compatibility under evaluation
properties.dimensions: Preliminary estimate, final dimensions not confirmed

properties.installationRequirements:
This is a preview specification for an unreleased, in-development product and must not be used to plan any live installation. All figures are preliminary engineering targets and are expected to change before general availability. The intended positioning is a step above the DX-360 for the highest-throughput logistics and highway sites, requiring an even larger dedicated MV/LV substation than the DX-360.

Routine preventive maintenance is recommended every twelve months for standard-duty sites, or every six months for sites averaging more than one hundred charging sessions per month, covering connector wear inspection, residual-current-device and breaker function testing, enclosure seal condition, and confirmation that the unit is running current firmware.
properties.safetyInformation: As an unreleased engineering sample, this specification is not validated for production installation and no safety certification has been completed. Any engineering-sample unit in a test environment must only be handled by qualified, certified personnel trained on high-voltage DC fast-charging prototypes, under controlled test-site conditions.
properties.certificationInformation: Not yet certified. Certification activity has not started; this document should not be interpreted as indicating any compliance status.

Internal draft documenting early DX-500 planning — a potential future addition above the DX-360 in the Nova DC line, aimed at the very highest-throughput logistics and highway sites. No launch date has been set and all specifications are subject to change or cancellation.
